statement: Sampling is the selection of a subset of individuals from within a statistical population to estimate characteristics of the whole population. The supplied sources contain no mathematical derivation or change_of_variables derivation, so sampling is treated strictly as a definition.

symbols.meaning: significance level used in sample size determination tables
type II error probability (related to power) used in sample size determination tables

properties.property: Sampling provides lower costs and faster data collection compared to a full census
properties.why: Measuring an entire population is often infeasible or impossible, whereas a representative subset can provide population insights

properties.property: Sampling schemes are classified as with replacement (WR) or without replacement (WOR)
properties.why: In WR an element may appear multiple times in the sample, whereas in WOR no element can be selected more than once

properties.property: Cluster sampling generally increases estimate variability compared to simple random sampling
properties.why: Variability increases depending on how clusters differ from one another relative to within-cluster variation, often requiring larger samples for equivalent accuracy

properties.property: Probability proportional to size (PPS) sampling concentrates sample selection on larger elements
properties.why: Selection probability for each element is set proportional to its size measure (up to 1), improving accuracy for estimates dominated by large elements

properties.property: Survey data require weighting when sample designs have unequal selection probabilities or varying stratum fractions
properties.why: Weighting compensates for unequal selection probabilities, non-response, or under-represented strata to ensure estimates correctly reflect the target population

assumptions.assumption: The statistical sample is representative of the target population
assumptions.breaks_when: Selection bias, under-coverage, non-response, or nonprobability sampling methods (such as convenience, voluntary, or haphazard sampling) cause the sample to systematically diverge from the population

assumptions.assumption: Assumed selection probabilities match the true selection probabilities
assumptions.breaks_when: Selection bias occurs in sample execution, leading to divergences between assumed design probabilities and actual selection probabilities

failure_modes.signature: Systematic divergence between sample estimates and true population parameters
failure_modes.cause: True selection probabilities differ from those assumed during design and analysis, or units are selected non-randomly

failure_modes.signature: Chance variation and dispersion in sample statistics across different draws
failure_modes.cause: Inherent variation caused by selecting a random subset rather than enumerating the entire population

failure_modes.signature: Biased parameter estimates due to incomplete data collection across the selected sample
failure_modes.cause: Selected individuals refuse to participate, cannot be contacted, or omit specific items, and non-respondents systematically differ from respondents

failure_modes.signature: Omission of population sub-groups or inclusion of ineligible units in sample estimates
failure_modes.cause: The sampling frame fails to encompass all population members or includes individuals outside the target population

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so sampling is recorded as a definition
